title: State justice and corrections grants to San Francisco
question: Who in San Francisco receives State justice and corrections grants, for what stated purpose, and do the nonprofit recipients carry warning signs?
finding: 36 awards worth $93.8 million are on file: $68.4 million to public agencies, led by San Francisco Police Department ($15.3 million: Suppression of Organized Retail Crime and Motor Vehicle Accessory Theft …), and $25.4 million to 18 nonprofit awards, led by Hunters Point Family ($5.0 million). 13 of the nonprofit awards went to organizations the City also pays, and 5 to ones carrying warning signs here: Hunters Point Family ($5.0 million); Juma Ventures ($4.5 million); Special Service For Groups Inc ($1.4 million); Five Keys Schools And Programs ($329,082).
how: Two State sources were joined: the award tables on the State corrections board's pages for its violence-prevention, Proposition 47 and Proposition 64 grants (rows naming San Francisco or a City-paid nonprofit), and the California Grants Portal rows for the corrections board, the prisons department, the Attorney General's office, the victim compensation board and the highway patrol, State fiscal years 2022-23 to 2024-25. An award found in both with the same amount is shown once. The stated goal is the project title and up to 22 words of the State's project description.
limits: A grant award is not a payment and says nothing about results. The corrections board's page tables do not print a cohort beside each row, so the cohort shown is read from the page layout and is approximate; some nonprofit rows serve several cities and the amount is for all of them. Evaluation reports for these grants exist on the board's site but are not on disk. Nonprofit recipients are matched to City payees and to warning signs by name only.
